target_name: Buyback Minus Dividend Intensity Under Profit
rationale: This is a re-scaled restatement of the archive's "Payout Permanence Mix" (sign-flipped) and overlaps "Repurchase Tilt Meets Free Cash Cover" and "Net Share Retirement Tilt," and because prstkc/at dominates dvt/at in cross-sectional variance the signal will largely reproduce the well-known net-repurchase/payout-yield anomaly conditioned on profitability rather than testing a new mechanism.

The extensive-margin decomposition is internally consistent (NEG makes profitable non-payers the long leg, matching the positive expected sign and the archive's negative dividend-share result), but the five-year payer count is nearly binary in practice, so the test effectively becomes "high-profitability non-payers vs. high-profitability payers" — a coarse and much-studied payer/non-payer contrast whose incremental content over the mix result is modest.

Removing the shared dvt term is a legitimate and well-motivated diagnostic of whether the archive's "Dividend Commitment Meets Cash Cover" alpha was mechanical, though the construction is a recombination of two existing archive legs and risks reducing to cash-flow profitability (oancf/at, a known anomaly) tilted toward dividend payers.

target_name: Own Cycle Timing Of Equity Flows
rationale: This is the archived "Peak-Profit Equity Issuance" interaction re-expressed with rank/z-score legs and a flipped sign, and the stated reasoning is self-contradictory — it claims to "adopt the data's direction" against the trough-conviction prior while the expression in fact implements exactly the trough-conviction ordering; additionally IND_RANK of net issuance discards the sign of the financing flow, silently deleting the repurchase side of the hypothesized interaction.

target_name: Clean Surplus Equity Flow Under Profit
rationale: The algebra correctly recovers net equity issuance from the clean-surplus identity, but that quantity is precisely Daniel–Titman (2006) composite equity issuance — a canonical published anomaly — and interacting it with profitability replicates the archive's existing profit x equity-flow signals; there is also a minor accounting mismatch in pairing dvt (total, including preferred) and ib (pre-preferred) with common equity.

The R&D-funding channel is genuinely new relative to the archive and the sign logic is coherent, but the claim that COALESCE-to-zero R&D "collapses non-innovators toward zero" is wrong — tied zero-R&D firms still receive a substantial common IND_RANK weight, so a large share of the resulting spread will simply be the known net equity issuance anomaly rather than the innovation-funding interaction.
